subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning the module structure, aiming for a moderately rich but efficient model with a simple joint hierarchy—chassis root, turret, and barrel—keeping the rigging minimal while avoiding API errors.

I'm sketching dimensions and placement: a 10m hull with a forward-elevated railgun barrel over the cab, six wheels positioned along the sides at ground level, and deployable stabiliser legs extending from the hull corners down to ground pads.

For materials I'm planning olive-mottled camo paint with textured details like emblems, hazard stripes, warning labels, and glowing cyan accents for the rail lights and coil rings. I'm also working out wheel construction with tires, hubs, and lug nuts, plus the precise z-coordinates for the front and rear axle pairs along the hull length.

Still laying out wheel positions and stabilizer leg placement, adjusting axle spacing to balance the cab, steering pair, and rear axle.

Now I'm building the hull geometry: a lower chassis box, rear deck box, cab box, and an angled windshield panel with a slight tilt, plus a cyan glow visor accent.

Adding the hood box in front of the cab, and extending the chassis length to accommodate both pieces. Then I'm setting up the turret, mounted on the rear deck with a ring joint and a body box sized for the mechanism.

Now I'm defining the turret's extruded side profile, then placing a gun joint with an 18° elevation pivot and starting the railgun's parallel barrel rails.

Adding glow panels, periodic clamp blocks along the barrel, a muzzle brake, a rear breech box, and turret-side capacitor cylinders with glowing cyan caps. Then I'm working out the gun elevation geometry so the barrel clears the cab, calculating the height at which it sits above the hull based on the pivot angle and barrel length.

Dropping elevation to 12° to get a cleaner tip height, and placing hydraulic elevation pistons as rods connecting the turret roof to the gun cradle. Now adding stabiliser legs mounted on either side of the hull near the front and rear, positioning the anchor points outward from the hull's centerline.

Working out the leg geometry: a hip joint attaches to the hull, an upper arm angles outward and up to a knee, and a lower leg drops down to an ankle, with each pair named per side and front/rear. I'm also adding a thinner chrome hydraulic piston rod running parallel to the leg for visual detail.

Now I'm designing the foot pads as low six-sided cylinders with a ball-joint sphere at the ankle, plus hazard-stripe texturing on top, and setting up named joints like "chassis" as the root and "wheelL1" etc. for spinning wheel bones parented to it. For the wheels themselves I'm defining tire cylinders oriented along the correct axis and starting to lay out a ring of tread blocks around the tire.

I'm adding a hub cylinder and lug nuts positioned trigonometrically around the wheel axis, then checking wheel placement so the bottom sits at y=0 and the wheels clear the hull sides. I'm also sizing mudguard boxes above the wheels and making sure the leg hip positions don't collide with the wheel radius given the body's width and the wheels' outward offset.

Now I'm working out fender placement over the wheel tops, shifting the stabilizer pads outward, and tallying total deployed width with legs extended. Then I'm sketching additional details: headlight glow boxes, a roof light bar, antenna rods, exhaust stacks, side storage boxes on the rear deck, a ladder, and an emblem decal.

For the decal I want a textured plane facing outward on the hull side, pulling in emblem, hazard stripe, number plate, warning sign, and radar screen textures from the clockwork kit's panelled paint system, then considering an olive/dark-olive mottled camo pattern with patches.

I'm settling on using patches with a dark olive base and lighter variant colors, then layering panelled camo with small rivets, keeping texel density reasonable since the painted area is large on this 14m model, and using metal paints like steel for rails and iron for the barrel.

Mostly flat colors with camo patches and metal paint for the barrel, keeping distinct colors under 64. I'm writing a small helper function for creating box geometry parts, then adding rear deck details like a cable reel, crates, ramp lights, tow hitch, and hazard stripes textured onto the stabiliser pads.

Now I'm placing a diagonal yellow-black hazard stripe texture, an emblem plane on the turret sides positioned relative to the turret's hull width, and dark side window planes on the cab based on its half-width.

I'm working out the vertical placement of the cab roof, rear deck, turret ring, hood, and chassis so they all align correctly in height and z-depth, then adding a front bumper box to cap off the chassis.

Now I'm adding details: a grille with horizontal bars in front of the hood, headlight glow points, and a tilted windshield box, working through the rotation math to get the windshield angled backward correctly.

I'm positioning a camera sensor with a lens glow on the turret, antenna rods at the rear deck corners, and exhaust stacks as vertical cylinders behind the cab with darkened tops.

Now I'm adding a flash hider at the muzzle and working out the capacitor bank placement on the rear deck, adjusting the turret's z-position to avoid it overlapping with the rear rack.

Checking the barrel's clearance over the cab roof at 12° elevation confirms it clears comfortably, and I'm fine-tuning the rack dimensions and position so it fits within the deck boundaries without colliding with the turret.

I'm defining the turret's cross-section outline for extrusion with sharp corners and camo coloring, then working out where the gun pivot sits relative to the turret front, checking that the cradle depth doesn't poke through the armor.

Now I'm laying out the gun assembly along its elevation direction, sizing the side rails and central barrel housing, positioning them relative to the pivot so the breech sits behind the roof line.

Adding clamps and glow strips...

Now I'm defining the position helper using pivot, direction, and up vectors, plus the leg hydraulics with hip, knee, and ankle joints and rod radii for the upper and lower leg segments.

Adding piston cylinder, mount block, ankle sphere, and foot pad geometry...

Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy for each leg—a hip joint parenting a knee joint, with separate upper and lower rod parts—then moving on to define wheel joints positioned relative to the chassis.

Modeling the tire, hub, rim, lug nuts, and hub cap as layered cylinders, with the tire's tread approximated by a ring of small boxes around the circumference rather than attempting curved geometry.

I'm deciding to skip the axle, differential, side skirts, fenders, and footstep details since they'd be mostly hidden or add unnecessary complexity, focusing instead on placing side tool boxes on the deck near the turret.

Adding rear tow hook, glowing red lights at the chassis rear, and a ramp bumper box. Setting up the color palette now with olive, dark, steel, iron, tire-black, cyan, yellow, red, glass, and tan tones, plus a camo paint patch system layered over the base olive color.

Adding the emblem, hazard stripes, nameplate, warning icon, and a glowing target-display texture for the rear rack, then setting up the plane geometry parts for mounting them.

Still writing helper functions...

Still defining joints...

Now I'm positioning the rack and screen near the rear face, adding vents on the sides, and considering whether to add deck rim details or hazard stripe edging on the pads and rear bumper.

Adding rear bumper geometry, chassis box, and underbody plating, then placing a roof light bar and sketching out a radar dish on the turret using a hemisphere shape...

Actually, I'll swap the radar dish for a sensor mast with a glowing cyan lens near the turret's left-top, and add capacitor cylinders on either side of the turret.

Now I'm realizing the turret emblem placement conflicts with those capacitors, so I should shift the capacitors lower or move the emblem to a gap on the hull side between the wheels instead.

Mapping out those gaps: there's a decent clearance between z -2.6 and 1.18, so the emblem can go around z -0.7 to -1.2 at a reasonable size, with the warning triangle placed separately near z 0.4-0.5, keeping both clear of the capacitor rack and wheel wells. I'll aim for roughly 330 lines total in the description and keep the build sheet under 40 lines.

Writing emblem and hazard-stripe SVG code...

Still writing SVG screen graphic...
